A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PerturbODE study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original SERGIO simulations, TF Atlas network recovery and held-out perturbation predictions, and supplementary resampling and gene-module analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and additionally evaluates Bicycle on the 100-gene simulated benchmark.

M1.justification: The sigmoid neural ODE, gene modules, decay and intervention terms, perfect-intervention masking, optimal-transport loss, sparsity penalty, and optional diffusion regularization are retained. Both fixed and tunable intervention-strength variants already appear in v1. The revised network notation G = A diag(alpha) B is equivalent to the earlier expression.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 400-gene yeast simulation, ten 100-gene random DAG simulations, and TF Atlas experiments, including the same held-out interventions and reduced 52-gene resampling analysis. Bicycle is evaluated within existing coverage.

E2.justification: Bicycle changes from a discussed method in v1 to an evaluated comparator on the 100-gene simulations in v3 Figures 2b and 9. The other comparator memberships are retained; Bicycle is explicitly excluded from larger benchmarks because of scalability.

E3.justification: v3 specifies settings for the added Bicycle comparison, including a 0.005 edge threshold. Section 4 also changes the stated sign-scoring rule: v1 treats predicted negative edges as absent, whereas v3 calls incorrect signs false positives. The retained thresholding description leaves implementation unclear, and this reported scoring change does not establish reruns. Existing data splits and simulation settings are retained.

E4.justification: v3 removes v1 Section 4.2.2's negative-autoregulation analysis and adds a Bicycle threshold-search finding in Appendix A.5. Existing perturbation-count, sparsity-penalty, module-count, resampling, enrichment, and prediction case analyses remain. Adding 'Power Analysis' to the appendix heading does not introduce a new analysis.

E5.justification: The reporting practices remain: mean/standard-deviation summaries, comparisons against 10,000 random graphs, 105 bootstrap resamples, and 133 train-validation splits. Bicycle's additional plotted results use existing reporting conventions. Removing the autoregulation p-value changes a result, while its statistical procedure remains described in Appendix A.3.

E6.justification: v3 adds Bicycle results showing AUPRC similar to PerturbODE and below DCDI on the 100-gene benchmark, but no tested threshold significantly outperforming random graphs at p <= 0.1. It removes v1's 26.4% negative-autoregulation finding and associated p < 0.001. Existing benchmark values and per-intervention errors are retained; AUPRC axis rescaling and reduced numerical precision do not establish performance changes.

T1.justification: New Section 5 assumes deterministic dynamics with stable fixed points and suggests identifiability up to permutation when interventions outnumber genes, appealing to an SDE result cited as Authors (2025). v1 left identifiability to future work. This adds conditional mathematical reasoning, but v3 still supplies no proof for the ODE case; existing derivations are retained.

C1.justification: The introduction replaces its headline contribution of novel diffusion-inspired regularization with prediction of unseen perturbations, which was already claimed elsewhere in v1. The principal claims of scalable, interpretable GRN discovery and trajectory prediction remain unchanged, and the regularizer itself is retained.

C2.justification: v3 adds the qualified identifiability discussion and proposes multimodal data to reduce false discoveries and multiple time points to distinguish direct from indirect effects. It removes the interpretation connecting negative autoregulation to biological realism. The limitations of incomplete reference networks and imperfect resampling consistency remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds Bicycle's implementation reference, threshold, learning rate, gradient clipping, and loss-weight settings. Conversely, v3 omits v1's explicit statement that intervention strengths generally default to ones. The existing preprocessing, ODE solver, SERGIO specifications, and PerturbODE hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: v3 expands positioning through PIDC, GENIE3, GRNBoost2, and Hossain et al.'s biologically informed neural ODEs, distinguishing their capabilities from multi-intervention causal modeling. It adds supporting references and the identifiability citation, while removing Schiebinger and Rosenfeld references. The central positioning combining causal discovery and cellular dynamics remains.

P1.justification: The main text undergoes extensive rewriting, particularly the introduction, related work, method explanations, and results narrative. Notation is revised, prediction and supplementary-results sections are reorganized, and Discussion, Acknowledgment, and Impact Statement sections are added. These changes substantially reshape the document's presentation despite largely retained scientific content.

P2.justification: The main text changes to two columns, with extensive figure and table restructuring. AUPRC panels become a combined main-text figure while thresholded metrics move to the appendix. The sparsity plot moves into the main text, module diagrams move into the appendix, and an existing IRF3 visualization and per-intervention table are redisplayed prominently. Table 1 is transposed and plot axes are revised.

improvement.justification: Evaluating Bicycle supplies a relevant cyclic comparator that v1 only discussed, making the empirical comparison more informative. Clearer positioning and prominent threshold and per-intervention displays also help readers assess the evidence. These are limited gains: the autoregulation evidence is removed, and the new identifiability discussion remains unproved and relies on an incompletely identified Authors (2025) citation.
